newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela June non-oil exports up 53 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela June non-oil exports up 53 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, rose $161 million, or 53.3 percent, to $463 million in June, from $302 million in June 1996, the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) said Wednesday.
Exports for the first six months of the year, at $2.297 billion, were up $392 million, or 20.6 percent, from $1.905 billion in the same period last year, the OCEI figures showed.
Exports in June were down $18 million, or 3.7 percent, from $481 million in May.
Non-traditional exports fell $274 million, or 6.1 percent, to $4.213 billion in 1996.

"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in the first six months of 1997 with 37.8 percent of total exports. "Chemical products" came next with a 15.7 percent share, then "transport materials" with 8.2 percent, "food, drinks and tobacco" with 7.1 percent, and "mineral products" with 5.1 percent.

Colombia was the chief market for Venezuela's non-traditional exports with 23.6 percent. Venezuela's next largest export market was the United States with a 22.7 percent share, followed by Japan with 4.3 percent, Mexico with 3.8 percent, the Netherlands with 3.7 percent, Ecuador with 3.4 percent, Brazil with 3.1 percent, and Peru with 3.0 percent.
